title: Jerry Valentine's fast arranging, the trombones and the rhythm section
summary: He describes trombonist-arranger Jerry Valentine, the changing trombone section, bassist Tommy Potter and guitarist Carney Wainwright.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And the trombone section... This is where my memory kind of goes blank. I can't remember, because that section changed around quite a bit. One of the main people in the trombone section that I remember was the arranger.... I don't know why I can't remember his name, because as well as I know it... Gerald Valentine! Jerry Valentine. Which is another guy that I learned a hell of a lot from about arranging. Jerry Valentine did most of the arrangements of the band. And I might add that he could write faster and come up with a good arrangement than anybody I've met yet. Because he could sit

down in a train station... Billy Eckstine would tell him, "We need an arrangement on so-and-so-and-so," and if we had a couple of hours to wait in the train station, he would sit down, and by that night, when we got to where we were going, he would have the arrangement. If we didn't play it on the bandstand that night, we'd rehearse it the next day. Sometimes he did it with a score, Other times he didn't use a score.

But I just couldn't... I never have been able to understand how he could do this, and come up with good arrangements, and no piano, nothing. He was a trombone player. Although he did play piano. He could play the piano, and he knew the piano well. But he only used it for arranging. A couple of times I heard him play a few things. As a matter of fact, I think he played piano with a group in Chicago, a small group, Dallas Bartley's band I think he played with, a guy that was formerly with Louis Jordan.

But to get back to the band. Jerry Valentine was a trombone player. And there was another r young fellow there, we used to call him Scotty -- I can't remember what his first name was. I think his last name was Scott, which is the reason why they called him Scotty. And the two other trombone players were a fellow we used to call Little Joe, another one was Taswell Baird, who was also from Kansas City. This other
trombone player, he had been formerly with Earl Hines, and I really can't remember his name. Maybe I'll think of it later.

But anyway, in the rhythm section was Tommy Potter on bass. The guitarist... The only guy that I know that could create almost exactly like Freddie Greene... Carney Wainwright was the guitar player. And I was the pianist, of course.
